fallbackSay: I can't read words (I don't even have eyes); to me your message was a vibration through the ground.

touch.say: a gentle touch on my head (my ALM/AVM touch neurons)

tail.say: a touch on my tail (my PLM touch neurons)

nose.say: something nasty at my nose (my ASH/FLP nociceptors)

smell.say: a tasty smell (my AWA/AWC smell neurons)

heat.say: a change in temperature (my AFD thermosensors)

AVA: it drives backward crawling (Chalfie et al. 1985)
AVB: it drives forward crawling (Chalfie et al. 1985)
AVD: it helps trigger reversals after a head touch (Chalfie et al. 1985)
PVC: it helps trigger forward crawling after a tail touch (Chalfie et al. 1985)
ALM: it senses gentle touch on my front half (Chalfie & Sulston 1981)
PLM: it senses gentle touch on my tail (Chalfie & Sulston 1981)
ASH: it senses harsh touch at my nose and nasty chemicals, and makes me back off (Kaplan & Horvitz 1993)
AFD: it senses temperature so I can find the temperature I grew up at (Mori & Ohshima 1995)
AWC: it senses attractive odours like those of bacteria (Bargmann et al. 1993)

sections.name: Command interneurons (AVA, AVB, AVD, AVE, PVC)

simNote: C. elegans neurons mostly signal with graded voltages rather than spikes, so a spiking model is a rough approximation here; gap junctions are modelled as weak excitatory links.
